title: Book Two · Chapter 87: Eleven at the Green Door
story:
It is late spring. Ronan's birthday comes again. He is eleven today. They still live behind the green door. The blue bike stands in the yard. It still has its old bell.

Dad asks Ronan to stand straight beside the inside wall. Mum holds a flat book above his head. Dad holds the pencil.

“Not on the door,” Mum says. “On this paper.”

She has fixed a narrow strip of paper to the wall. Dad makes a small mark on it and adds eleven beside the line.

Ronan steps away and looks. The mark seems high. He stands under it again, this time on his toes.

Mum puts one finger on his shoulder.

“Both feet flat.”

“I am practising for next year.”

Dad raises the pencil. “Then I need a longer paper.”

They laugh. Mum takes the strip down after they check the mark. Ronan keeps it inside his own book. It belongs to him. He likes to keep his height mark.

At breakfast, he gets noodles again. This year, Dad draws a cake that stands straight. There are eleven candles, but one flame looks like a bird.

“That one can fly away,” Ronan says.

“Eat before the rest do,” Mum says.

His present is a small pencil case. The old one still holds pencils, but its corner is worn through. Ronan moves the wooden bead and string to the new case. The bead knocks softly against the side.

He opens both cases on the table. A short pencil has gone through the old corner. Mum lifts the case so he can see its point.

“That is where it went.”

“I thought I lost it.”

Ronan puts the pencil with the others. He leaves the little pieces of dust on the old cloth, away from his noodles.

Dad watches him tie the bead again.

“Another year for that one.”

Ronan turns it between two fingers. It has no new colour and no birthday number. He still likes the way it knocks against the case.

He closes the new case and puts the old one beside it.

“Can I keep this too?”

“Of course,” Mum says.

Ronan lays his little rubber inside the old case for now. It cannot fall through the narrow hole so easily. Then he checks the knot on the new one before he puts the present safely away.

Later, Leo and Jun meet him at the square. Mei comes for a little while with her own family nearby. They play a game with the ball, then sit in the shade. It is his birthday. But anyone can win the game.

Jun wins the final round anyway. He gives Ronan a very deep bow. Ronan throws the ball toward Jun's feet. Jun catches it on the way down.

At home, Mum has a customer collection before supper. Ronan keeps the game things clear of her path. The customer takes the finished clothes and leaves on time.

Then the family can use the table. Dad sets out a small extra dish. Mum chooses the window seat. Ronan sits opposite her. His new case is beside his bowl.

“Do you feel eleven?” Dad asks.

Ronan thinks about it. His knees still fit under the table. His bowl is still the small one.

“A little.”

Mum puts another spoonful into his bowl. “Try that.”

He tastes it and nods very seriously. Dad asks for some eleven too. Mum gives him a very tiny spoonful.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

eleven＝十一；pencil＝铅笔；mark＝记号。

## 理解问题

1. 十一岁生日怎样明确发生？
2. Ronan与父母怎样测量并保留身高记号？

## 读句子

**Dad / holds / the pencil.** Dad／拿着／铅笔。
